title: You're Kidding!
subtitle: Four more ways to say you can't believe it
review: Written by Claude: check the English lines, the notes and the questions. No Burmese yet.
intro: A cat accused of stealing the ham, a suspiciously clean apartment, a Sunday race and a lottery win: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for the difference between 'I'm amazed' and 'I don't believe a word of it', and for how the other one insists.

lines.text: You're not going to believe this. It was the cat.
lines.note: You're not going to believe this: say it before surprising news.
Yeah, right is sarcastic. It means 'I don't believe you'.

lines.text: I swear! He opened the fridge.
lines.note: I swear! = I promise it is true.

lines.text: Give me a break. He can't even use his cat door.
lines.note: Give me a break = stop, I don't believe that. Can't even: it makes the no stronger.

lines.text: I saw it with my own eyes.

lines.note: Just watched: you did nothing else.
In shock: too surprised to move.

lines.text: As if! Did he put the plate in the dishwasher, too?
lines.note: As if! = that is not possible.
Good manners: polite behavior.

lines.text: I don't believe it! You vacuumed?
lines.note: Vacuum: clean the floor with a machine.
No way! here means 'I'm amazed', not 'you're lying'.

lines.text: The blue vase. But look how the floor shines.
lines.note: Look how…: look at the way…

lines.text: I signed us up for a race on Sunday.
lines.note: Sign up for: put your name on the list.

lines.text: Not at all. It starts at eight.
Are you kidding me? On a Sunday?
lines.note: Are you kidding me? is stronger than You're joking.

lines.text: You can't be serious. We never run! How far is it?
lines.note: How far: asks about distance.

lines.text: One mile. It's the family fun run.
lines.note: A fun run: a short race for everyone, not for champions. One mile = 1.6 kilometers.
For real? = really? Informal.

lines.text: And there's a chocolate medal at the finish line.
You should have started with that.
lines.note: Should have + past participle: it was the better thing to do.

lines.text: Holy cow! Emma! We won the lottery!
lines.note: Holy cow!: strong surprise, friendly, not rude.

lines.text: It's true! Look at the numbers!

lines.note: Hold on = wait.
Insane: even stronger than crazy.

lines.text: Unbelievable. And how much did you spend on tickets?
lines.note: Here Unbelievable is sarcastic: her voice is flat.
Still: even so.

notes: Real surprise: I don't believe it!, No way!, Unbelievable!, That's impossible!, That's crazy!, Holy cow!
Checking that it is not a joke: You're joking, right?, Are you kidding me?, You can't be serious, For real?
Not believing a word: Yeah, right, Give me a break, As if! The voice is slow and flat.
Insisting: I swear!, It's true!, Believe me, I saw it with my own eyes.
Tone changes the meaning: Unbelievable! can be real surprise or sarcasm.
You're not going to believe this comes first, before the surprising news.

questions.q: Lucas says the cat opened the fridge. Emma does not believe him. What does she say?
questions.why: Yeah, right is sarcastic: 'I don't believe you'.

questions.q: Lucas wants Emma to believe him about the cat. What does he say?
options: I saw it with my own eyes.
questions.why: I saw it with my own eyes = I was there, so it is true.

questions.q: The apartment is clean. Emma is amazed. What does she ask next?
questions.why: She thinks Lucas cleaned because he broke something. He did: the blue vase.

questions.q: Emma signed them up for a race. Lucas thinks it is a joke. What does he say?
questions.why: You're joking, right? checks that it is not a joke.

questions.q: Lucas spent ten dollars and won six. What does he say?
options: You should have started with that.
questions.why: Still = even so. He lost four dollars, but he is happy.
